mainTopic: רבן גמליאל's stringencies on יום טוב (insulating, the מנורה) and the limits on extinguishing and medical treatment on יום טוב and שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation of why רבן גמליאל's household did not insulate hot food on יום טוב for שבת. The first approach is that no עירובי תבשילין was made, and only a few basics are allowed; a ברייתא supports this list. רבא says instead that there was an עירוב, but insulating clearly shows it is for שבת. אביי rejects this from חנניה's version of בית שמאי and explains that the person made an עירוב for baking and cooking but not for insulating. Next, the גמרא explains that standing up a sectioned מנורה looks like building, which בית שמאי forbid for כלים. A story about עולא's servant tilting a lamp teaches that making a flame go out sooner counts as extinguishing. A series of questions follows about putting out a lamp or a fire on יום טוב for privacy or to save property, and about putting medicine on an eye; each is forbidden according to the רבנן. Each time, the ברייתא about the smoky log is explained as רבי יהודה's view. Finally, אמימר allows a גוי to treat an eye on שבת, because a helper's minor help counts for nothing. רב אשי then challenges his eye treatment on the second day of ראש השנה, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The list of allowed basics ends: lighting a lamp
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier statement listing the small things that may be done for someone who did not make עירובי תבשילין: they may also light a lamp for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they may light a lamp for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list it began just before this section. The list covers what may still be done for a person who forgot to make עירובי תבשילין. The last item is lighting a lamp for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list explains the משנה as a case where no עירוב was made. Even then, a few minimal things are allowed so that he has the basics for שבת, including one insulated pot. In this approach, בית שמאי did not allow even that single pot, and רבן גמליאל's household was strict like them.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'mixing of cooked foods' set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

phrases.english: And they light the lamp for him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the person who forgot his עירוב; this line finishes a list that began just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of allowances given in the earlier answer, before this section begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even for someone without עירובי תבשילין, a lamp may be lit for him for שבת.

steps.title: רבי יצחק adds roasting a small fish
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי יצחק, they added one more allowed item: roasting a small fish for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said in the name of רבי יצחק: they may even roast a small fish for him.
steps.whatsHappening: An extra opinion is added to the list of allowed basics. According to רבי יצחק, one may also roast a small fish for the person who has no עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' ('even') shows this goes one step further than the basic list. A small fish counts as a minimal food for שבת, so it fits the same idea of giving him only the bare necessities.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Yitzchak they said:
They may even roast a small fish for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more item to the list from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יצחק, one may also roast a small fish for someone who has no עירובי תבשילין.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the list of allowed basics
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same list: one loaf, one insulated pot, a lamp, and one jug of hot water. Some also add a small fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: for someone who did not make עירובי תבשילין, they may bake one loaf for him, insulate one pot for him, light a lamp for him, and heat one jug of water for him. Some say they may even roast a small fish for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as the earlier statement. This supports it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that even without an עירוב, a person is allowed a few single items: one loaf, one pot and one jug. Its 'יש אומרים' matches רבי יצחק's small fish exactly. This supports the approach that the משנה is about someone who made no עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this (a support)
they insulate (wrap food to keep it hot)

steps.whatToRemember: Even with no עירובי תבשילין, a person may get a few single basics for שבת: one loaf, one pot, a lamp and one jug of hot water. Some add a small fish.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
One who did not set aside an eiruv tavshilin,
they bake one loaf for him,
and they insulate one pot for him,
and they light the lamp for him,
and they heat one jug for him,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף צוֹלִין לוֹ דָּג קָטָן.
phrases.english: and some say: they may even roast a small fish for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting the list in steps 1 and 2.
steps.raayaObject: The list of minimal allowances for someone without עירובי תבשילין, including רבי יצחק's small fish.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that gives the same list and cites the small fish as 'יש אומרים'.

steps.title: רבא: there was an עירוב, but insulating is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the משנה differently. The person did make an עירוב, but insulating is still special. It clearly shows that he is working for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: really, the case is where he did make an עירוב. Insulating is different, because it is obvious that he is doing it with שבת in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new way to understand the משנה. In his view, the person did make an עירוב, and the problem is something special about insulating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baking or cooking on יום טוב could be for יום טוב itself. Wrapping food to keep it hot overnight, though, is plainly for tomorrow, which is שבת. Since it so clearly prepares for another day, בית שמאי (followed by רבן גמליאל) forbid it even when there is an עירוב.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Actually, it is where he did set one aside,
phrases.notes: He means he did make the עירובי תבשילין, unlike the earlier approach.

phrases.english: but insulating is different,
because the matter is evident
that he is doing it with Shabbat in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the משנה's case than steps 1 to 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case in the משנה and explains it with a special reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once an עירוב is made, insulating should be allowed like baking and cooking.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with an עירוב, insulating is forbidden for בית שמאי, because it clearly shows the work is for שבת.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from חנניה's version of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes חנניה: according to בית שמאי, each activity needs its own matching עירוב. For insulating, that means hot food already insulated from ערב יום טוב. So insulating is allowed when the right conditions are met, even though it obviously is for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: חנניה says that בית שמאי say: one may not bake unless he made an עירוב with bread. One may not cook unless he made an עירוב with a cooked dish. One may not insulate unless he had hot food insulated from ערב יום טוב. This means that if he did have hot food insulated, he may do it, even though it is obvious he is doing it for שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation. He brings a source showing that בית שמאי do allow insulating when the right preparation was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said insulating is forbidden because it so clearly prepares for שבת. But חנניה reports that בית שמאי allow insulating if he already had hot food insulated from before יום טוב. So 'obviously for שבת' cannot be the reason it is forbidden. The real issue is only whether the right kind of עירוב was made.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection against him (from a source)
from the day before יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: For בית שמאי there is no single all-purpose עירוב. Each activity needs its own matching one: bread for baking, a cooked dish for cooking, and insulated hot food for insulating.

phrases.english: Abaye objected to him:
Chananya says: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹפִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵרֵב בְּפַת,
phrases.english: One may not bake unless he made an eiruv with bread,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְבַשְּׁלִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עֵרֵב בְּתַבְשִׁיל,
phrases.english: and one may not cook unless he made an eiruv with a cooked dish,
and one may not insulate unless

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לוֹ חַמִּין טְמוּנִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: he had hot food insulated from the eve of the Festival.
So if he had hot food insulated,
he may in any case do it,
even though the matter is evident
that he is doing it with Shabbat in mind!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reason in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that insulating is forbidden because it clearly shows the work is for שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנניה's report of בית שמאי allows insulating when hot food was insulated before יום טוב, even though it is still obviously for שבת. So that cannot be the reason it is forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: he made an עירוב for one activity but not the other
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the משנה as a case where the person made an עירוב for baking and cooking but not for insulating. The משנה follows חנניה's version of בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: the case is where he made an עירוב for this but not for that. It follows חנניה, according to בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבא's approach, אביי gives his own explanation of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following חנניה, בית שמאי require a separate matching עירוב for each activity. In the משנה, the person made an עירוב for baking and cooking but had no hot food insulated from before יום טוב. So he may bake and cook, but not insulate. רבן גמליאל was strict like this view of בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: for this one but not for that one

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's conclusion: the משנה follows חנניה's version of בית שמאי. Each activity needs its own matching עירוב, so a person who had no insulated food from before יום טוב may not insulate, even if he may bake and cook.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the reason behind רבן גמליאל's strictness. It is not that insulating looks like preparing for שבת. It is that insulating needs its own matching עירוב.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
For example, where he made an eiruv for this,
phrases.notes: 'This' means baking and cooking: he set aside bread and a cooked dish for them.

phrases.english: but did not make an eiruv for that,
phrases.notes: 'That' means insulating: he had no hot food insulated from before יום טוב.

phrases.english: and it is the view of Chananya,
according to Beit Shammai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's rejected explanation with a new one built on the source used in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case in the משנה and links it to a specific view (חנניה's version of בית שמאי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Insulating is forbidden because it is obviously for שבת (רבא).
steps.terutzMaskana: Insulating is forbidden only because no matching עירוב was made for it, following חנניה's version of בית שמאי.

steps.title: What is wrong with standing up a fallen lamp?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next stringency in the משנה, not standing up a מנורה, and asks what forbidden act this involves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one may not stand up the lamp.' What forbidden thing is the person doing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next of רבן גמליאל's strict rulings in the משנה and asks what is wrong with it. This is a setup question; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking up a lamp that fell over does not look like any forbidden מלאכה. So the גמרא needs to find what prohibited act could be involved.

keyTerms.meaning: what is he doing? (what forbidden act?)

phrases.english: And one may not stand up the lamp.
What is he doing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the insulating case (הטמנה) to the next item in the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which forbidden מלאכה is involved in setting up a fallen מנורה on יום טוב.

steps.title: A lamp made of pieces looks like building
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר ביסנא explains that the case is a lamp made of separate sections. Putting it together looks like building, which בית שמאי forbid for כלים and בית הלל allow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר ביסנא said: Here we are dealing with a lamp made of sections, and putting it together looks like building. בית שמאי hold that building applies to utensils. בית הלל hold that building does not apply to utensils, and taking apart does not apply to utensils either.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חיננא בר ביסנא answers the question. The משנה is talking about a lamp that comes apart in pieces, and putting the pieces back together looks like building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not lifting the lamp. The problem is joining its sections back together. This depends on a מחלוקת: בית שמאי say the prohibition of building applies to כלים, while בית הלל say neither building nor taking apart applies to כלים.

keyTerms.meaning: sections or segments that fit together

steps.whatToRemember: Standing up a sectioned מנורה is a בית שמאי stringency, because they hold there is building with כלים. בית הלל hold there is no building or taking apart with כלים.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of whether בנין and סתירה apply to כלים comes up again and again in הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥinnana bar Bisna said:
Here we are dealing with a lamp made of sections,
which looks like building.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי: יֵשׁ בִּנְיָן בְּכֵלִים,
phrases.english: For בית שמאי hold: there is building with utensils,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי: אֵין בִּנְיָן בְּכֵלִים
phrases.english: and בית הלל hold: there is no building with utensils
and there is no taking apart with utensils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מנורה is made of sections, and reassembling it looks like building. This is forbidden according to בית שמאי, who hold there is building with כלים.

steps.title: עולא's servant tilts a lamp in רב יהודה's house
steps.stepSummary: עולא visited רב יהודה, and עולא's servant tilted the lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא happened to come to רב יהודה's house. His servant got up and tilted the lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a lamp on יום טוב. This sets up רב יהודה's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tilting the lamp moves the oil away from the wick, so the flame goes out sooner. The question will be whether that counts as putting out a fire.

phrases.english: עולא happened to come to the house of רב יהודה,
his servant got up and tilted the lamp.
phrases.notes: Here זְקַף means tipping the lamp so the oil runs to one side, away from the wick, and it burns out faster.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the word זקף again, but now in a story about making a lamp go out early.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: עולא's servant tilted a burning lamp on יום טוב.

steps.title: Making a lamp go out faster counts as extinguishing
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה challenges עולא with a ברייתא: taking oil out of a burning lamp makes one liable for extinguishing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה objected to עולא: One who puts oil into a lamp is liable for kindling, and one who takes oil from it is liable for extinguishing!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה uses a ברייתא to show that what the servant did was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking oil out of a lamp does not put the flame out right away. It only makes the lamp go out sooner, yet the ברייתא still calls it מכבה. Tilting the lamp away from the oil is the same thing, so it should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him from a source

phrases.english: רב יהודה raised an objection to עולא:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹתֵן שֶׁמֶן בַּנֵּר — חַיָּיב מִשּׁוּם מַבְעִיר,
phrases.english: One who puts oil into a lamp is liable for kindling,
and one who takes oil from it is liable for extinguishing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the servant's act in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The tilting of the lamp done in עולא's presence.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making a lamp burn out sooner counts as extinguishing, as the ברייתא shows with removing oil. So tilting the lamp is forbidden.

steps.title: עולא: it was done without my knowledge
steps.stepSummary: עולא agrees the act was wrong and says his servant did it without his knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: It was not with my knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers by admitting the point. He did not approve of what his servant did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא does not argue with the ברייתא. He agrees that tilting the lamp is forbidden and only explains that he was not responsible for it.
steps.whatToRemember: Making a lamp go out sooner, even without directly putting out the flame, counts as מכבה. עולא agreed.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was not with my knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב יהודה's objection by agreeing with it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the law is accepted, and the act is blamed on the servant acting alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It might seem that עולא allowed tilting the lamp on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא agrees it is forbidden. His servant acted without his knowledge.

steps.title: רב permits trimming the burnt wick
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that trimming the burnt end of a wick on יום טוב is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Trimming the burnt end of the wick is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a short ruling related to lamps on יום טוב. Trimming the charred tip of a wick is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after learning that making a lamp go out sooner is forbidden, we learn a case that is permitted. Trimming the burnt part helps the lamp burn better, and it is not considered extinguishing.

keyTerms.meaning: the burnt, charred end of a wick

phrases.english: Rav said: Trimming the burnt end of the wick is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a permitted lamp-related act after the forbidden one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trimming the charred end of a wick on יום טוב is permitted.

steps.title: May one put out a lamp for marital privacy?
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא asks אביי whether one may put out a lamp on יום טוב for the sake of 'another matter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא בר מרתא asked אביי: What is the law about putting out a lamp because of 'another matter'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about putting out a lamp on יום טוב for a personal need. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, some מלאכות are allowed for a real need. The question is whether this need, privacy for marital relations, is enough to allow putting out a lamp.

keyTerms.meaning: 'another matter,' a polite way of saying marital relations

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּא בַּר מָרְתָא מֵאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: אבא בר מרתא asked אביי:
What is the law about putting out the lamp
because of 'another matter'?
phrases.notes: 'Another matter' is a modest way of saying marital relations, which should not take place with a lamp lit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּא בַּר מָרְתָא מֵאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of putting out lamps on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting out a lamp on יום טוב is allowed for marital privacy.

steps.title: אביי: use another room instead
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that it is forbidden, because one can go to another room.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is possible in another room.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says not to put out the lamp, because the couple can use a different room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is another way to meet the need without doing a מלאכה, the need does not allow putting out the lamp on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's first answer: do not put out the lamp, because another room is available. The following steps show that the ban does not actually depend on such alternatives.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is possible in another room.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אבא בר מרתא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is forbidden to put out the lamp, since one can use another room.

steps.title: What if there is no other room?
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא follows up: what if the person has no other room to go to?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does not have another room, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: אבא בר מרתא pushes back on אביי's answer by asking about a person who has no second room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had said the lamp may not be put out because the person can simply go to another room. Now the question tests what happens when that easy way out is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: another room (here, another room in the house)

phrases.english: If he does not have another room, what then?
phrases.notes: This continues the question from before: putting out the lamp on יום טוב for marital privacy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question that removes the solution אביי gave in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting out the lamp becomes allowed when there is no second room.

steps.title: He can put up a partition
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that he can set up a partition instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible to make a partition for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second way to get privacy without putting out the lamp: put up a divider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי still does not allow putting out the lamp. He only swaps in another solution, a מחיצה, which separates the couple from the light.

phrases.english: It is possible to make himself a partition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 with another alternative.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Set up a partition instead of putting out the lamp.

steps.title: What if he cannot make a partition?
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא asks: what if he has nothing to make a partition with?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has nothing to make a partition with, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: אבא בר מרתא removes the second option too and asks again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each question takes away the solution just offered. The goal is to see whether, at some point, putting out the lamp becomes the only choice and is therefore allowed.

phrases.english: If he has nothing to make a partition with, what then?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the partition option from step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting out the lamp is allowed when no partition can be made.

steps.title: He can cover the lamp with a vessel
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that he can turn a vessel upside down over the lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible to turn a vessel over on top of it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a third option: cover the lamp with an overturned vessel to block the light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering the lamp hides the light, and the flame is not deliberately put out. So אביי keeps finding ways to avoid putting out the flame.

keyTerms.meaning: to turn upside down over something

phrases.english: It is possible to turn the vessel over on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 with a third alternative.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cover the lamp with an overturned vessel.

steps.title: What if he has no vessel?
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא asks the final follow-up: what if there is no vessel either?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does not have a vessel, what should he do?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last question in the chain. Every alternative has now been removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no other room, no partition and no vessel. The question is whether, with no way out, the lamp may finally be put out.

phrases.english: If he does not have a vessel, what then?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the last alternative from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting out the lamp is allowed when no alternative exists at all.

steps.title: Still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that even with no alternatives, putting out the lamp is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his bottom line: no matter what, he may not put out the lamp on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the alternatives were never the real reason for the ban. Putting out a flame for this purpose is simply not allowed on יום טוב in אביי's view.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ban depended on having another room or a vessel. Those were just practical suggestions. Even when none are available, אביי still forbids it.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final answer to the chain of questions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Putting out the lamp is forbidden even when no alternative exists.

steps.title: Challenge from the burning log
steps.stepSummary: אבא בר מרתא challenges אביי with a ברייתא that allows putting out a log so the house or pot won't get smoky.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: One may not put out a log to save it, but if it is so the house or pot will not get smoky, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא בר מרתא quotes a ברייתא that seems to allow putting out a fire for a person's comfort, which goes against אביי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids putting out a log just to save the wood. But it allows it to keep smoke out of the house or pot. If putting out a fire is allowed to avoid smoke, why not for privacy?

keyTerms.meaning: a piece of firewood, a log
to spare it, to save it from burning up

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: אבא בר מרתא is challenging אביי here.

phrases.english: One may not put out a log
in order to save it,
but if it is so that the house will not get smoky
or the pot — it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's ruling in step 20 from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that putting out the lamp is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows putting out a fire for a person's comfort (avoiding smoke), so it should be allowed for privacy too.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, but his own ruling follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That follows רבי יהודה; when I spoke, I meant according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes the challenge aside by saying the ברייתא reflects a different opinion from the one he follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows more on יום טוב than the רבנן do, so under his view putting out the log is fine. אביי rules like the רבנן, who are stricter, so the ברייתא does not disprove him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָהִיא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: He said to him: That one is רבי יהודה;
when I said it, it was according to the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to a different opinion (רבי יהודה) than the one the ruling follows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is everyone's view, so putting out a fire for comfort is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only רבי יהודה; according to the רבנן it is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי forbids putting out a lamp on יום טוב for privacy, even with no other choice. The ברייתא that allows putting out a log against smoke is only רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: Putting out a house fire on יום טוב to save property
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה whether one may put out a fire on יום טוב when only money, not life, is at stake.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: May one put out a fire on יום טוב? Where life is in danger I have no question, since even on שבת it is allowed. My question is when only property would be lost — what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question on the same subject: can you put out a fire on יום טוב to stop property from burning?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי first narrows the question. Danger to life is obviously allowed, even on שבת. So the real question is only about losing money (אבוד ממון).

phrases.english: אביי asked of רבה:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְכַבּוֹת אֶת הַדְּלֵקָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: What is the law about putting out a fire on יום טוב?
Where there is danger to life —
I have no question,
since even on שבת it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָמִבַּעְיָא לִי מִשּׁוּם אִבּוּד מָמוֹן, מַאי?
phrases.english: When I ask, it is about loss of property — what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related question about putting out fires on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may put out a fire on יום טוב to prevent only a loss of property.

steps.title: רבה forbids it
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that putting out a fire to save property on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rules that you may not put out the fire just to save property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saving money is not enough of a reason to put out a fire on יום טוב. Only danger to life permits it.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Putting out a fire on יום טוב only to prevent loss of property is forbidden.

steps.title: Same challenge from the burning log
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with the same ברייתא about the log and the smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: One may not put out a log to save it, but if it is so the house or pot will not get smoky, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the same ברייתא against רבה that was brought against himself earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you may put out a log just so the house or pot won't be damaged by smoke, which is a small loss, surely you may put out a fire to prevent a bigger loss.

phrases.english: He challenged him: One may not put out a log
phrases.notes: This time it is אביי challenging רבה.

phrases.english: in order to save it,
but if it is so that the house will not get smoky
or the pot — it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's ruling in step 24 with the ברייתא from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that putting out a fire to save property is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows putting out a fire to prevent smoke damage, a small loss, so preventing a larger property loss should be allowed too.

steps.title: Again: that is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, while his ruling follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That follows רבי יהודה; when I spoke, I meant according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the same answer אביי gave before: the ברייתא is רבי יהודה's opinion, not the one he follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By assigning the ברייתא to רבי יהודה, רבה keeps his ruling standing according to the stricter רבנן. Both rulings in this section, אביי's and רבה's, rest on the same answer.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא רבי יהודה, who allows more on יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, a fire may not be put out on יום טוב for privacy or to save property; only danger to life allows it. The ברייתא about the smoky log follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: That one is רבי יהודה;
phrases.notes: רבה is the one answering here, even though the words "he said to him" are left out.

phrases.english: when I said it, it was according to the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 the same way as step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to a different opinion (רבי יהודה) than the one the ruling follows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that putting out a fire to prevent loss is allowed by everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי יהודה allows it; according to the רבנן, putting out a fire for property loss is forbidden.

steps.title: May one put medicine on the eye on יום טוב when there is no danger?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר about painting the eye with medicine on יום טוב. He says that dangerous eye illnesses are clearly allowed even on שבת, so he is only asking about milder cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked אמימר: What is the law about putting medicine on the eye on יום טוב? When there is danger, like the illnesses רירא, דיצא, דמא, דמעתא, קדחתא, or the start of an inflammation, I have no question, because even on שבת it is allowed. My question is about the end of an inflammation, or putting medicine on just to make the eyes sharper. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks אמימר a narrow question: may one put medicine on an eye on יום טוב when the eye is not in danger?
steps.deeperAnalysis: He first takes the easy cases off the table: real eye danger is allowed even on שבת, so of course on יום טוב. The real question is about mild cases, where only comfort or better sight is at stake. This matches the earlier questions about doing forbidden work on יום טוב for a bodily need that is not a matter of life.

keyTerms.meaning: To paint the eye — putting ointment or medicine on the eye
An eye inflammation (it 'eats' at the eye)
Brightening the eye — making eyesight sharper
I have no question about this

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked Ameimar:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לִכְחוֹל אֶת הָעַיִן בְּיוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: What is the law about painting the eye with medicine on a Festival?
Where there is danger, for example:
rira, ditza, dema, dimata, and kadachta,
phrases.notes: These are names of eye illnesses that are serious enough to put the eye in danger.

phrases.english: and the beginning of an inflammation

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִבַּעְיָא לִי, דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת שְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: I have no question, because even on Shabbat it is permitted.
Where I do have a question
is the end of an inflammation, or brightening the eye — what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי מֵאַמֵּימָר: מַהוּ לִכְחוֹל אֶת הָעַיִן בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in the same pattern as steps 23–26: forbidden work on יום טוב for a bodily need when there is no danger to life.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether putting medicine on an eye on יום טוב is allowed for mild cases (end of inflammation, sharpening sight) where there is no danger.

steps.title: אמימר forbids it
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that putting medicine on the eye on יום טוב in these mild cases is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives a short answer: in the mild cases, it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is no danger, this is only for comfort or better sight. אמימר does not allow forbidden work on יום טוב for that kind of need.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Putting medicine on the eye on יום טוב for mild, non-dangerous cases is forbidden.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges from the ברייתא about the burning log
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר from the same ברייתא about putting out a burning log, which allows putting it out to prevent smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection to him: 'One may not put out a burning log' (but one may put it out so the house will not get smoky).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks אמימר's ruling using the same ברייתא about the burning log that was used twice before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows putting out a log so the house or pot won't get smoky, which is just a bodily comfort. If forbidden work is allowed on יום טוב for that kind of comfort, then putting medicine on an eye for comfort should also be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from a ברייתא or משנה)
A piece of burning wood, a log

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: One may not extinguish a log,
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא from before; its second half allows putting out the log so the house won't get smoky.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's answer in step 28, repeating the challenge of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that eye medicine on יום טוב for a mild case is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows putting out the log to avoid smoke, a mere bodily comfort, so forbidden work for bodily comfort should also be allowed here.

steps.title: אמימר gives the same answer as before
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers just as רבה and אביי did before: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, but his own ruling follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he answered him the way we answered before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא doesn't spell out the answer again; it says אמימר answered just as was answered earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer was that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who is more lenient on יום טוב. אמימר rules like the רבנן, who forbid it, so the ברייתא is no problem for him.

phrases.english: And he answered him as we answered before.
phrases.notes: Look back at steps 22 and 26: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, while the ruling follows the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29 with the same answer given in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different opinion (the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be the accepted halacha, allowing work for bodily comfort.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only רבי יהודה's view; אמימר rules like the רבנן, so mild eye treatment stays forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: For mild eye problems with no danger, אמימר forbids putting medicine on the eye on יום טוב, following the רבנן.

steps.title: אמימר allowed a גוי to put medicine in an eye on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that אמימר allowed a גוי to put medicine on a Jew's eye on שבת. Another version says אמימר himself had his eye treated this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר allowed having a גוי paint the eye on שבת. Some say: אמימר himself had his eye painted by a גוי on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new story: אמימר allowed using a גוי to treat an eye on שבת. This sets up רב אשי's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the question was a Jew doing the work himself; now a גוי does it. There are two versions: one says אמימר only ruled it was allowed, the other says he actually did it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say — introducing a second version

phrases.english: Ameimar permitted painting an eye
by means of a gentile on Shabbat.
Some say:
Ameimar himself had his eye painted
by a gentile on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר שָׁרֵי לְמִכְחַל עֵינָא מִגּוֹי בְּשַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: using a גוי for eye treatment on שבת, rather than a Jew doing it on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי may put medicine on a Jew's eye on שבת (according to one version, אמימר did this himself).

steps.title: רב אשי suggests the source for אמימר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר for his reasoning and suggests it: עולא said all needs of a sick person may be done by a גוי on שבת, and רב המנונא said that for anything without danger, one may tell a גוי to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: What is your reasoning? Is it because עולא son of רב עילאי said: All the needs of a sick person may be done by a גוי on שבת; and רב המנונא said: For anything that has no danger, one tells a גוי and he does it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks אמימר why he allowed this and offers the likely source. This is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two teachings support אמימר: עולא lets a גוי do all the needs of a sick person, and רב המנונא lets one ask a גוי when there is no danger. רב אשי accepts these sources, but he is preparing to show they don't fit אמימר's case.

keyTerms.meaning: The needs of a sick person
He tells the גוי and the גוי does it

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
What is your reasoning?
Is it because Ulla son of Rav Ilai said:
All the needs of a sick person
may be done by a gentile on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: He means a sick person whose life is not in danger; if life were in danger, even a Jew could do it.

phrases.english: and Rav Hamnuna said:
Anything in which there is no danger,
one tells a gentile, and he does it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and suggests the source behind אמימר's ruling in step 31, as setup for the challenge in step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source אמימר relied on to allow a גוי to treat an eye on שבת; רב אשי suggests עולא and רב המנונא.

steps.title: But you are helping the גוי by closing and opening your eye
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that those sources only allow it when the Jew does not help the גוי at all, but אמימר helps by closing and opening his eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only when the Jew does not help the גוי. But you, Master, help him, because you close and open your eye!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי now challenges אמימר: the permission to use a גוי works only if the Jew does nothing, and here אמימר is taking part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the patient closes and opens his eye, it helps the medicine go in, so the Jew is sharing in the work. If the Jew is part of the act, it is no longer purely the גוי's work, so the sources from עולא and רב המנונא should not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only — limiting a rule
Helps him, assists along with him

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלָא מְסַיַּיע בַּהֲדֵיהּ.
phrases.english: This applies only where he does not help him.
But the Master is helping him,
phrases.notes: 'The Master' is a polite way of saying 'you,' meaning אמימר.

phrases.english: since he closes and opens his eye!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דְּלָא מְסַיַּיע בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the sources from step 32 to challenge the ruling of step 31, by showing that they only cover a case where the Jew does not help.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's permission (or practice) of having a גוי paint the eye on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Asking a גוי is allowed only when the Jew does not take part; closing and opening the eye is taking part, so it should be forbidden.

steps.title: A helper's minor help counts for nothing
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that רב זביד already asked the same question, and he answered him that a person who only helps a little adds nothing real to the act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב זביד also holds like you, and I answered him: A helper's help counts for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers רב אשי's challenge: רב זביד once asked the same thing, and he answered that minor help is not considered doing the work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי is the one really doing the work; the patient closing and opening his eye is just a small extra. Since the help is so minor, the Jew is not counted as doing the work, so the permission to use a גוי still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Who holds like you, who takes your position
A helper adds nothing real — minor help does not count as doing the work

steps.whatToRemember: A Jew may have a גוי treat a non-dangerous illness on שבת, and small help from the patient, like closing and opening the eye, does not make it forbidden: מסייע אין בו ממש.
steps.confusionAlert: אמימר is not saying a Jew may do forbidden work on שבת. The גוי does the work; the Jew's small help is simply not counted as doing it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מסייע אין בו ממש, that minor help counts for nothing, comes up in other places in the laws of שבת as well.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיכָּא רַב זְבִיד דְּקָאֵי כְּוָתָךְ,
phrases.english: He said to him: There is Rav Zevid, who holds like you,
phrases.notes: He means רב זביד raised this exact same challenge to him before.

phrases.english: and I answered him:
A helper has no substance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיכָּא רַב זְבִיד דְּקָאֵי כְּוָתָךְ, וְשַׁנַּיי לֵיהּ: מְסַיֵּיעַ אֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the Jew's action as too minor to count as taking part in the work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Closing and opening the eye makes the Jew a partner in the forbidden work, so the permission to use a גוי should not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: Minor help adds nothing real (מסייע אין בו ממש), so the act counts as the גוי's alone and stays permitted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Having a גוי treat the eye on שבת is permitted even though the patient closes and opens his eye, because a helper's minor help counts for nothing.

steps.title: אמימר permits eye treatment on the second day of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: אמימר allowed putting medicine on an eye on the second day of יום טוב of ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר allowed putting medicine on an eye on the second day of ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story about אמימר and eye medicine, this time on the second day of ראש השנה. This story sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier story (Step 31), the eye treatment was done on שבת by a גוי. Here the day is different: the second day of יום טוב of ראש השנה. The question now becomes how strict that second day is.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting medicine or ointment (כּוֹחַל) on the eye
The second day of יום טוב
The new year festival, which is kept for two days

phrases.english: Ameimar permitted painting an eye
phrases.notes: "Painting" here means smearing healing ointment on a painful eye.

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: on the second day of Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about אמימר and eye treatment. It moves from שבת with a גוי to the second day of ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting medicine on an eye is allowed on the second day of יום טוב of ראש השנה.

steps.title: רב אשי quotes רבא on burial during יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר by quoting רבא: on the first day of יום טוב, non-Jews should handle a dead body, and on the second day, Jews may. This applies even to the two days of ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But רבא said that if someone dies on the first day of יום טוב, non-Jews take care of him. On the second day, Jews take care of him. This is true even on the two days of ראש השנה...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts a challenge against אמימר by quoting a rule of רבא about burial on יום טוב. The challenge is not finished yet. The next words of the גמרא will complete it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא treats the second day of יום טוב more lightly than the first: Jews may bury the dead on it. He stresses that this is true even for ראש השנה. רב אשי is using this statement to question how אמימר treated the second day of ראש השנה. The exact point of the attack comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: "But didn't he say?" A standard way to open a challenge from an earlier source
The אמורא whose ruling is being quoted
They should attend to him, that is, handle his burial

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי's quote is not over at the end of this line. The point of the challenge comes in the next words of the גמרא, so don't decide yet what his question is.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar,
But didn't Rava say:
If someone died on the first day of Yom Tov,
non-Jews should attend to him,
phrases.notes: "Attend to him" means taking care of the burial.

phrases.english: on the second day of Yom Tov,
Jews may attend to him.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: And this is so even on the two days of Yom Tov of Rosh Hashanah,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר, וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling in Step 35 using a statement of רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's permission to treat an eye on the second day of ראש השנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's rule about how the second day of יום טוב is treated, even on ראש השנה, is brought to question אמימר's ruling. The exact contrast is finished in the following line.
